openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Cloudy air, Venus's day. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Wide chest, slow pulse, open hands. Close days reward the person who is calm at 11:10 — that's you.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Friday is Venus's day — vendredi, viernes. Venus rules finish, form, and what you are willing to let go. The window you opened yesterday has a hard edge at 11:11. You don't extend it. You don't refresh it. You close it clean and leave the afternoon for the body and the board. Competitive. Unbeatable. One breath, one close, one clean finish. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Friday: run this right after Morning Charge — breath first, then the body. About 53° and cloudy outside; get warm before the screens. Then the close check.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

items.hed: GeoInt: an open-source skill that places a photo
items.body: Posted this morning. It reads signs, plates, plants, and light, runs reverse-image search plus local vision models, compares Street View, and returns coordinates with a confidence score and sources. Free. Built for Codex and Claude Code.
Also final: Heat 128–Pelicans 118, Celtics 124–Cavaliers 113, Hawks 123–Spurs 116, Nets 114–76ers 108, Wizards 111–Knicks 109.
Tampa Bay (1-4) picked up its first win Thursday night in Dallas. Cowboys fall to 2-3. Sunday noon CT: Bears (3-1) at Packers (2-2), Chicago listed at -1.5.
In the planetary week Friday is Venus's day — vendredi, viernes. English named it for Frigg. Venus rules form, finish, attraction, and the art of stopping. A close is a Venus act.

On the Tree of Life, Venus sits at Netzach, endurance and beauty. Its pair is Hod (Mercury), structure and language. The teaching: a clean end is as much a win as a loud start. The 11:11 close is Netzach. The copy you already wrote is Hod.

grimoire.hed: There is a time to keep, and a time to cast away
grimoire.body: Ecclesiastes, in the Solomonic line: a time to keep, and a time to cast away. Yesterday you kept the window open. Today you cast the offer away on purpose, at the hour you set. That is not loss. That is the seal.
grimoire.practice: After four rounds of box breathing, say out loud: 'The window closes at 11:11. I do not extend it.' Check the page once. At 11:13, close the tab. Then the opener is already done — leave the body warm and the screen dark.

lesson.oneLiner: A photo is a case file. Read the clues, check them against maps, then say how sure you are.
beats: Read it: signs, plates, buildings, plants, and the light — not just the landmark.
Check it: reverse-image search plus vision models on your own machine, then Street View panoramas.
Weigh it: an evidence board, coordinates, a confidence level, and the sources behind the answer.
Use it: same shape as a deal note. Claim, proof, confidence. No vibe-only close.
lesson.takeaway: Show the sources. @mmmik000: if you can't point at the proof, you don't have a location — you have a guess.
